note: Wall-clock and machine-dependent: recorded, not asserted. Every round of every figure is kept (roundFields says what each column of a round is); the medians, quartiles and verdicts beside them are computed from the rounds by bench/lib/codec-verdict.cjs, and tests/bench/ts-codec-verdict.test.ts recomputes them. A cell is measured in-process (three stores in one process) and per-process (three fresh processes, one codec each); its verdict is the per-process one.

rules.quartiles: the element at index floor(q * n) of the sorted paired differences

readsRetaken.rule: A basis of a cell whose A/A control was outside +-2% or whose peak load reached 6 in the full run was taken once more, in a run of those cells alone (--reads with --only); the re-take replaces the figure in the cell and the first take stays inside it as firstTake. A re-take is not repeated, so a re-take whose control is still out of band reads inconclusive.

nativeSmallestFirst.note: Cells of the mixed and spread8k intersects, measured both ways like every read cell. vsShipped: the subjects are native as shipped (the `native` column), native with the smallest-first operand order (the column named `typescript`, which here is that native codec) and a second native as shipped (the control); its typescriptVsNative is therefore the effect of the order on the native codec, paired round by round. tsVsSmallestFirstNative: the subjects are native with the smallest-first order, the TypeScript codec and a second smallest-first native (the control).

memory.order: native first on even repeats, TypeScript first on odd ones
